sn44.7:1.1: See [sn33.1:1.2]() and note for Vacchagotta. | This discourse introduces the full set of ten undeclared points.
sn44.7:2.1: _Loka_ originally meant “light”, hence the sky bright with gods (stars), from which developed the meanings “heaven”, a “world”, and the “cosmos”. Sometimes Vedists believed that an “eternal world” was won by those worthy ([dn1:1.31.5]()). However, the Suttas often discuss the Upaniṣadic notion that the “self and the cosmos are eternal” ([dn1:1.30.1](), [mn102:14.2]()), where _loka_ means the “cosmos” as a whole, not a specific heavenly “world”. But the distinction is not always clear-cut. See also next note.
sn44.7:2.7: The distinction between a limited “world” and an infinite “cosmos” was said to depend on the wisdom and spiritual depth of the individual: “Those who venerate (water, breath, and moon) as finite win only a limited world, whereas those who venerate them as infinite win a world without limit” (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.5.13, Olivelle translation).
sn44.7:2.13: The term “soul” (_jīva_) was favored by the _samaṇas_, as opposed to the “self” (_attā_) of the brahmins. Both are rejected by the Buddha as forms of “metaphysical” self: they postulate the absolute, eternal existence of entities that cannot be established empirically. The repeated demonstrative pronouns (_taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ_) assert an emphatic identity.
